newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo board says to decide on mills '98.
newsitem.headline: MoDo board says to decide on mills '98.

text.p: The board of Swedish forestry group MoDo AB said on Wednesday that a decision about the possible expansion of the Husum plant and the future of the Domsjo mill will be made in the autumn of 1998.
The board was reiterating comments made by MoDo chief executive Bengt Pettersson on December 6.
The board also said in a statement that the Domsjo mill is not for sale.

The MoDo mill posted a loss of around 50 million crowns from January to November this year, including positive hedging effects, MoDo said. Excluding foreign currency hedging, the loss amounted to about 115 million crowns, the company said.
Pettersson last week said making the decision in 1998 gave the company time to finalise internal research about the situation.
The whole issue of whether to close the Domsjo mill and expand the close by Husum mill arose on October 7 this year when Pettersson launched the idea.

On December 6, Pettersson repeated his view that both investments and raw material supplies should be concentrated to one unit to enable creating a long-term and internationally viable industrial structure in the Ornskoldsvik region.
"I mean that this unit should be Husum," he said at the time, adding that an expansion application will be filed with environmental authorities next spring.
